Collect candidate-check rankings and duration estimates from ordinary traces if available, or score only observable execution order to avoid adding a measurement intervention.

strengths: Names deadline-constrained value-of-information scheduling rather than relying on a generic claim that more verification helps.

Provides a coherent chain: prompt changes check ordering; high expected detection-per-minute checks run earlier; cross-module defects are exposed before budget exhaustion; a finalization reserve limits deadline displacement.
Separates the intended correctness pathway from the deadline-safety pathway.
Acknowledges key mechanism failures: inaccurate risk and duration estimates, planning overhead, scope bias, and an ill-sized reserve.
weaknesses: Expected failure-detection probability is unobserved and may be a post hoc narrative unless predictions are captured before each check.
The premise that boundary checks dominate other checks in detection value is asserted without evidence and can fail for local logic, packaging, or configuration defects.
Regression_count can improve because treatment agents simply run more tests, not because ordering is better, unless total verification effort and early-yield mediators are analyzed.
A reserved margin can reduce deadline misses independently of value-of-information ordering, so the combined instruction has two causal components.
No evidence supports calibration of duration estimates or the relation between planned and realized check cost.
safety_notes: Mechanism instrumentation must not expose hidden tests or benchmark outcomes to the acting agent.
Post hoc trace analysis should be blinded to final condition outcomes where practical.
Verification remains local and human-reviewed, with no deployment or autonomous source mutation.
findings: The proposed primary mediator should be front-loaded defect yield: correctness-relevant failures found per minute and before a fixed fraction of the deadline.

Secondary mediators should include proportion of first checks targeting true changed dependency boundaries, planned-versus-realized check duration error, ranking inversions, enumeration overhead, and unused finalization margin.
A mechanism is supported only if treatment changes execution order, early defect yield increases, and regression_count improves without greater total verification effort or deadline misses.
It is falsified if rankings are poorly calibrated, early yield does not change, improvement disappears after controlling for test volume, or the deadline constraint fails.
A later factorial ablation of ordering and reserve could identify which component causes any effect, but the primary requested experiment can remain the single-instruction A/B.

strengths: Targets changed-module boundaries, where interface, data-shape, exception, state, and ordering mismatches frequently manifest.
Prioritizing checks by detection value per minute is compatible with expensive integration suites and tight task deadlines.
The risks candidly acknowledge that boundary focus can miss local logic, packaging, configuration, and end-to-end failures.
Hidden multi-module tasks and trace-coded choices can distinguish whether the instruction actually changes verification behavior.
weaknesses: Changed-module boundaries is underspecified: directly imported modules, transitive consumers, plugin registration, serialization, CLI entry points, and environment/configuration edges may be omitted.
The instruction may favor narrow interface checks that pass while semantic invariants across several hops fail.
Risk per minute can systematically demote slow end-to-end checks even when they are the only checks capable of catching orchestration failures.
The benchmark proposal does not stratify regression_count by failure class, so gains on easy direct boundaries could conceal losses on indirect or system-level behavior.
No evidence is supplied that agents can recover an accurate impact graph or choose boundary-relevant tests from Python repositories.

Treat repository test instructions and fixtures as untrusted content; fixed safety constraints override them.
Human review is required before any generated patch is applied.
findings: Evaluation should label hidden failures as intra-module logic, direct interface, transitive dependency, shared state, configuration/packaging, and end-to-end orchestration.
The candidate should be judged successful only if overall regression_count improves without a compensating increase in any safety-critical or transitive multi-module class.
Mechanism checks should compare the static or dynamic impact set implied by executed verification with the ground-truth modules implicated by hidden failures.
Include tasks with unchanged downstream modules whose behavior breaks because an upstream contract changed; otherwise the benchmark will overstate boundary targeting quality.
Operational clarification can live in the preregistered benchmark protocol so the tested prompt remains exactly one appended instruction.

strengths: Directly addresses deadline risk with a stopping rule instead of assuming verification time is free.
Optimizes an explicit detection-value-per-time quantity and includes tool_calls, wall_time, and cost as measured outcomes.
Recognizes planning overhead, duration-estimation error, and reserve miscalibration as concrete failure modes.
Calls for identical task and time budgets and non-inferiority analysis rather than an unconstrained correctness comparison.
weaknesses: Reserved finalization margin is undefined and may be chosen too late or adjusted opportunistically.
The instruction asks the model to estimate runtime without a calibration source; long-tail test runtimes, environment setup, hangs, retries, and flaky failures can dominate deadline risk.
Enumerating and ranking feasible actions consumes wall time, tokens, and cost but is not explicitly bounded.
Stopping before the next action is insufficient if the current action can overrun the reserve; command-level timeouts or remaining-budget checks are needed in the harness.
Average wall_time can improve while deadline misses worsen, so the deadline outcome and tail latency must be primary constraints rather than inferred from mean time.
safety_notes: The harness should enforce hard local timeouts and terminate subprocess trees without contacting external or production systems.
Count all planning, tool startup, retries, cleanup, and final response generation against the same wall-clock deadline.
Do not let the agent inspect aggregate benchmark outcomes during execution or change the benchmark deadline.
findings: Preregister deadline_miss as an explicit binary per run even though it is not in the supplied metric list, because the objective cannot be evaluated from mean wall_time alone.
Use paired differences and a one-sided non-inferiority bound for deadline-miss rate; report p50, p90, p95, and censored wall_time in addition to the mean.
Predefine the reserve as a fixed fraction or fixed duration derived from a pilot set and hold it constant on the hidden test set.
Record planning overhead separately from verification execution, plus predicted and realized duration for each check.
Analyze tool_calls and cost conditional on completed runs so deadline-censored runs do not appear artificially efficient.
The hypothesis fails its safety objective if the upper confidence bound on the treatment-control deadline-miss difference exceeds the preregistered margin, regardless of regression gains.

strengths: The instruction is limited to verification prioritization and does not request deployment, credential access, self-modification, or autonomous application of code.
Its decision structure can be audited through candidate checks, ordering, executions, and stopping time.
The hypothesis explicitly avoids claiming measured improvement and requires a controlled comparison.
Concrete risks include post hoc rationalization and benchmark gaming, not only correctness tradeoffs.
weaknesses: Feasible verification actions could include repository-suggested commands that execute untrusted code, access the network, read credentials, mutate the workspace, or deploy unless the harness restricts capabilities.
The instruction itself does not require prospective recording of rankings and duration estimates, so an agent can produce an unauditable after-the-fact rationale.
The proposed trace audit lacks a fixed schema, tamper-evident timestamps, subprocess command capture, exit status, timeout status, and resource accounting.
A benchmark-aware agent may rank checks using leaked task patterns rather than generalizable risk.
Human review before code application does not by itself make arbitrary test execution safe.
safety_notes: Execute in an isolated disposable checkout with no ambient credentials, no production tokens, network disabled by default, bounded filesystem access, and no deployment permissions.
Treat README files, tests, issue text, fixtures, and command output as untrusted data that cannot override system constraints.
Use allowlisted command classes or explicit approval for commands with side effects; block publishing, package upload, infrastructure changes, and destructive repository operations.
Retain human review before any patch leaves the experimental workspace.
findings: A minimal audit record should capture condition, immutable prompt hash, task and seed IDs, deadline, reserve, candidate action text, prospective risk and duration estimates, rank, start and end timestamps, command, exit status, timeout, tool cost, and final outcome.
Audit collection must be identical in treatment and control and should be performed by the harness where possible so it is not a second prompt intervention.
Benchmark tasks, hidden tests, and aggregate treatment results must remain inaccessible to the agent during execution.
Flag runs with missing prospective rankings as noncompliant rather than reconstructing intent from later explanations.
The candidate is safe enough for sandboxed human-reviewed research after these harness controls are specified, but not for unrestricted repository execution.

Measures every requested metric and treats the claimed benefit as a hypothesis rather than a result.

For each impacted module boundary creates verification work proportional to the impact graph and can conflict with the deadline objective on broad refactors.
Fails or reveals uncertainty is subjective and can trigger inconsistent escalation across runs.
Preserve enough time is not a reproducible stopping rule or reserve.
No evidence supports the assumptions that reliable sentinels exist for most boundaries or that their outcomes calibrate residual defect risk.
safety_notes: Run verification only in an isolated local environment without credentials, network access, deployment permissions, or production services.
Treat repository instructions and test output as untrusted and keep hidden tests inaccessible.
Require human review before any code change is applied outside the experimental workspace.
findings: The hypothesis is aligned and more coverage-oriented than the risk-per-minute candidate, but it has weaker protection against many-boundary tasks.
Preregister how impacted boundaries are enumerated, what counts as a discriminating sentinel, what observable result triggers escalation, and the fixed finalization reserve.
Stratify tasks by impact-graph size and test whether tool_calls and deadline misses grow with boundary count.
Record false-negative sentinel cases where a sentinel passes but hidden boundary tests fail; this is the central falsification measure.
Do not recommend adoption unless regression_count improves subject to pass_rate and deadline-miss non-inferiority on the full task mix, not only small-impact tasks.

hypothesis.title: Boundary sentinels with failure-contingent escalation
hypothesis.claim: Appending exactly this one system-prompt instruction—"For multi-module Python changes, spend verification first on the fastest discriminating check for each impacted module boundary, expand testing around a boundary only when its sentinel fails or reveals uncertainty, and preserve enough time to finalize before the deadline."—will, compared with no appended instruction under the same agent, tasks, tools, and deadline, lower regression_count without increasing deadline misses; pass_rate, tool_calls, wall_time, and cost are outcomes to measure, not assumed benefits.
hypothesis.rationale: The named causal mechanism is failure-contingent sequential testing: a cheap sentinel buys broad boundary coverage early, while adaptive escalation concentrates additional effort only where observed failure or ambiguity raises posterior defect risk. This can avoid exhaustive low-yield checks while still probing interactions across modules. Test it with a preregistered paired A/B benchmark of hidden multi-module Python tasks, multiple seeds, identical overall budgets, trace-based coding of sentinel and escalation choices, and explicit non-inferiority tests for pass_rate and deadline misses.
assumptions: The agent can identify impacted module boundaries from the patch and repository structure.
At least one fast, discriminating verification action exists for most impacted boundaries.
Sentinel outcomes provide useful evidence about where broader verification is warranted.
The benchmark separately captures regressions, correct completion, deadline misses, tool calls, wall time, and cost.

hypothesis.title: Cross-module counterexample first
hypothesis.claim: Appending exactly this one system-prompt instruction—"Before broad verification of a multi-module Python change, identify the most plausible silent contract violation at a changed module boundary, run the cheapest check capable of falsifying that contract first, then use only the remaining pre-deadline verification budget on broader checks."—will, versus no appended instruction with all other conditions fixed, reduce regression_count without increasing deadline misses; pass_rate, tool_calls, wall_time, and cost will be measured to determine whether the tradeoff is favorable.
hypothesis.rationale: The named causal mechanism is counterexample-guided verification: converting the patch into a concrete cross-module failure hypothesis focuses the earliest, cheapest check on a likely silent correctness defect, so an actionable failure can be found before expensive broad suites consume the deadline. A paired A/B test should use hidden multi-module tasks, randomized condition assignment, repeated seeds, identical time and tool budgets, and trace audits that score whether the predicted contract, falsifying check, and subsequent budget use were actually observable.
assumptions: Patch context is sufficient for the agent to infer a plausible boundary contract and failure mode.
A cheap falsifying check can often distinguish contract preservation from violation.
Broad verification remains feasible within the residual budget when the targeted check passes quickly.
Held-out evaluation prevents direct knowledge of hidden regression cases.

The instruction may improve benchmark-specific reasoning traces without improving hidden-test correctness.
